texts: When resynchronisation fails because the left ventricular epicardial lead sits too far forward, the best next step is another epicardial lead placed more laterally, over the latest-activated wall.
In left bundle branch block the lateral and posterolateral wall contracts last, and a lead on the anterior wall cannot correct the dyssynchrony.
She meets the criteria for CRT, an ejection fraction of 25% and left bundle branch block with a QRS of 165 ms, so a correctly placed lead is likely to help.
Raising the output of a badly placed lead does not move the point of stimulation, and switching to the other existing lead does not reach the lateral wall either.
Referral for transplant comes only after CRT and medical therapy have failed.
In the picture, Franky nails a new drumstick on the far side wall of the red room, and the two drummers finally beat together.
Memory hook: the drummers agree only when the stick is on the far wall.
